 EXHIBIT 99.1
 Exhibit 99.1 
 Li Auto Inc. Announces Unaudited Third Quarter
2026 Financial Results 
 Quarterly total revenues reached RMB28.8 billion
(US$4.3 billion) 1 
 Quarterly deliveries were 99,964 vehicles
 BEIJING, China, November 25, 2026 — Li Auto
Inc. (“Li Auto” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq: LI; HKEX: 2015), a leader in China’s new energy vehicle market,
today announced its unaudited financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.
 Operating Highlights for the Third Quarter of 2026 
 | · | Total deliveries for the third quarter of 2026 were 99,964 vehicles, representing a 7.2% year-over-year
increase. | 2026 Q3 | 2026 Q2 | 2026 Q1 | 2025 Q4 | Deliveries | 99,964 | 98,330 | 95,142 | 109,194 | 2025 Q3 | 2025 Q2 | 2025 Q1 | 2024 Q4 | Deliveries | 93,211 | 111,074 | 92,864 | 158,696 | · | As of September 30, 2026, in China, the Company had 485 retail stores in 160 cities, 532 servicing centers
and Li Auto-authorized servicing shops operating in 217 cities, and 4,188 super charging stations in operation equipped with 23,077 charging
stalls. | 
 Financial Highlights for the Third Quarter of 2026 
 | · | Vehicle sales were RMB27.1 billion (US$4.0 billion) in the third quarter of 2026, representing
an increase of 4.7% from RMB25.9 billion in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 12.6% from RMB24.1 billion in the second quarter
of 2026. | · | Vehicle
 margin 2 was 15.3% in the third quarter
 of 2026, compared with 15.5% in the third quarter of 2025 and 9.4% in the second quarter
 of 2026. | · | Total revenues were RMB28.8 billion (US$4.3 billion) in the third quarter of 2026, representing
an increase of 5.4% from RMB27.4 billion in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 12.3% from RMB25.7 billion in the second quarter
of 2026. | · | Gross profit was RMB4.8 billion (US$718.3 million) in the third quarter of 2026, representing an
increase of 7.8% from RMB4.5 billion in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 69.8% from RMB2.8 billion in the second quarter of
2026. | · | Gross margin was 16.7% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with 16.3% in the third quarter of
2025 and 11.0% in the second quarter of 2026. | · | Operating expenses were RMB5.5 billion (US$822.7 million) in the third quarter of 2026, representing
a decrease of 2.3% from RMB5.6 billion in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 7.4% from RMB5.1 billion in the second quarter
of 2026. | 
 1 
All translations from Renminbi (“RMB”) to U.S. dollars (“US$”) are made at a rate of RMB6.7045 to US$1.00, the
exchange rate on September 30, 2026 as set forth in the H.10 statistical release of the Federal Reserve Board. 
 2 
Vehicle margin is the margin of vehicle sales, which is calculated based on revenues and cost of sales derived from vehicle sales only.

 | · | Loss from operations was RMB699.6 million (US$104.4 million) in the third quarter of 2026, representing
a decrease of 40.6% from RMB1.2 billion in the third quarter of 2025 and a decrease of 69.6% from RMB2.3 billion in the second quarter
of 2026. | · | Operating margin was negative 2.4% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with negative 4.3% in
the third quarter of 2025 and negative 9.0% in the second quarter of 2026. | · | Net loss was RMB309.7 million (US$46.2 million) in the third quarter of 2026, representing a decrease
of 50.4% from RMB624.4 million in the third quarter of 2025 and a decrease of 81.8% from RMB1.7 billion in the second quarter of 2026.
 Non-GAAP net loss 3 was RMB112.9 million (US$16.8 million) in the third quarter of 2026, representing a decrease of 68.6%
from RMB359.7 million in the third quarter of 2025 and a decrease of 92.5% from RMB1.5 billion in the second quarter of 2026. | · | Diluted
 net loss per ADS 4 attributable to ordinary shareholders was RMB0.32 (US$0.05)
 in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB0.62 in the third quarter of 2025 and RMB1.69
 in the second quarter of 2026. Non-GAAP diluted net loss per ADS attributable to ordinary
 shareholders was RMB0.12 (US$0.02) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB0.36
 in the third quarter of 2025 and RMB1.49 in the second quarter of 2026. | · | Net cash provided by operating activities was RMB3.2 billion (US$481.6 million) in the third quarter
of 2026, compared with RMB7.4 billion net cash used in operating activities in the third quarter of 2025 and RMB15.0 million net cash
provided by operating activities in the second quarter of 2026. | · | Free cash flow 5 was RMB2.0 billion (US$292.6 million) in the third quarter of 2026,
compared with negative RMB8.9 billion in the third quarter of 2025 and negative RMB1.3 billion in the second quarter of 2026. | 
 3 
The Company’s non-GAAP financial measures exclude share-based compensation expenses. See “Unaudited Reconciliation of U.S.
GAAP and Non-GAAP Results” set forth at the end of this press release. 
 4 Each ADS represents two Class A ordinary shares. 
 5 
Free cash flow represents operating cash flow less capital expenditures, which is considered a non-GAAP financial measure.

 3 
 Recent Developments 
 Delivery Update 
 | · | In October 2026, the Company delivered 29,025 vehicles. As of October 31, 2026, in China, the Company
had 481 retail stores in 159 cities, 527 servicing centers and Li Auto-authorized servicing shops operating in 217 cities, and 4,206 super
charging stations in operation equipped with 23,163 charging stalls. | 
 Product Lineup Update 
 | · | In September and October 2026, the Company launched the new Li MEGA, a high-tech flagship MPV, Li i9,
a pioneering flagship family SUV, and 2026 Li i6, a pioneering five-seat SUV. These models feature the Company’s latest proprietary
technologies, including the MACH M100 chip and Lianshan Battery, together with other premium configurations. The new Li MEGA, Li i9, and
2026 Li i6 are priced at RMB509,800, RMB369,800, and RMB249,800, respectively. Deliveries of the new Li MEGA and Li i9 began in September,
and deliveries of the 2026 Li i6 began in October. | 
 Equity Financing for Chip Business 
 | · | On October 16, 2026, the Company announced the equity financing for Shanghai Mahe Xin Technology Co.,
Ltd. (“MHX Technology”), a subsidiary of the Company dedicated to its chip and domain controller business. The Company, through
a wholly-owned subsidiary, and external investors will invest RMB1.0 billion and RMB625 million respectively in MHX Technology. Further
details are available in the Company’s announcement published on the website of HKEX on October 16, 2026. | 
 US$1.0 Billion Share Repurchase Program 
 | · | Pursuant to its US$1.0 billion share repurchase program announced on March 24, 2026, the Company repurchased
a total of 10,638,200 Class A ordinary shares at an aggregate consideration of HK$493.3 million on the HKEX and a total of 13,562,312
ADSs (representing 27,124,624 Class A ordinary shares) at an aggregate consideration of US$169.7 million on the Nasdaq in the third quarter
of 2026. As of the date of this press release, the Company has repurchased a total of approximately 102.3 million Class A ordinary shares
(including approximately 23.7 million ADSs) for an aggregate consideration of approximately US$694.4 million. | 
 Global Expansion 
 | · | The Company reached new globalization milestones, launching its all-new Li L9 in the UAE in September
2026, making its European premiere at the Paris Motor Show in October 2026, and signing agreements with partners across Hong Kong, Thailand,
Singapore, the Philippines, and Vietnam in November 2026 to advance its Asia-Pacific expansion. The Company plans to debut the right-hand-drive
Li MEGA at the Thailand International Motor Expo and launch it in Hong Kong in December 2026, followed by the start of deliveries of Li
6 (the Europe-spec Li i6) in the Netherlands and Norway in the first quarter of 2027. | 
 Power Day 
 | · | In October 2026, the Company hosted Power Day to introduce its proprietary Lianshan Electric Technology
System, covering battery, electric drive, and charging infrastructure. The Company also launched the Lianshan Battery Warranty Program
at the event, further underscoring its commitment to user experience and confidence in its proprietary electric technologies. | 
 4 
 CEO and CFO Comments 
 Mr. Xiang Li, chairman and chief executive officer
of Li Auto, commented, “The strength of our proprietary technologies, from the MACH M100 chip to the Lianshan Battery, is increasingly
reinforcing our competitive moat. Through our user-centric, integrated software-hardware iteration, these capabilities enable tighter
system integration that delivers differentiated user experiences while enhancing our supply chain resilience. This ultimately translated
into stronger delivery performance in the third quarter. Looking ahead, we remain committed to advancing frontier technologies to transform
user experiences and drive industry progress.”
 Mr. Tie Li, chief financial officer of Li Auto,
added, “Despite ongoing industry-wide cost headwinds, our gross margin continued to improve sequentially, reaching 16.7% in the
third quarter, and free cash flow turned positive. This performance reflects the strength of our optimized product mix, the efficiency
gains from our proprietary technologies, and continued operational discipline. With an updated product lineup and ongoing advancements
in our in-house technologies, we are well-positioned to navigate market dynamics and further strengthen our financial performance. Going
forward, we will maintain our steadfast investments in deepening our technological moat and advancing global expansion, driving our next
phase of growth and creating incremental shareholder value.”
 5 
 Financial Results for the Third Quarter of 2026 
 Revenues 
 | · | Total revenues were RMB28.8 billion (US$4.3 billion) in the third quarter of 2026, representing
an increase of 5.4% from RMB27.4 billion in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 12.3% from RMB25.7 billion in the second quarter
of 2026. | · | Vehicle sales were RMB27.1 billion (US$4.0 billion) in the third quarter of 2026, representing
an increase of 4.7% from RMB25.9 billion in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 12.6% from RMB24.1 billion in the second quarter
of 2026. The increase in revenue from vehicle sales over the third quarter of 2025 was primarily due to the increase in vehicle deliveries,
partially offset by a lower average selling price due to a different product mix. The increase in revenue from vehicle sales over the
second quarter of 2026 was primarily attributable to a higher average selling price due to a different product mix. | · | Other sales and services were RMB1.7 billion (US$259.6 million) in the third quarter of 2026, representing
an increase of 16.2% from RMB1.5 billion in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 8.8% from RMB1.6 billion in the second quarter
of 2026. The increase in revenue from other sales and services over the third quarter of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026 was mainly
due to increased provision of services and sales of accessories, which is in line with higher accumulated vehicle sales. | 
 Cost of Sales and Gross Margin 
 | · | Cost of sales was RMB24.0 billion (US$3.6 billion) in the third quarter of 2026, representing an
increase of 4.9% from RMB22.9 billion in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 5.2% from RMB22.8 billion in the second quarter
of 2026. The increase in cost of sales over the third quarter of 2025 was primarily due to the increase in vehicle deliveries and a higher
average cost of sales due to a different product mix, partially offset by estimated costs related to the recall of Li MEGA in the third
quarter of 2025. The increase in cost of sales over the second quarter of 2026 was primarily attributable to a higher average cost of
sales due to a different product mix. | · | Gross profit was RMB4.8 billion (US$718.3 million) in the third quarter of 2026, representing an
increase of 7.8% from RMB4.5 billion in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 69.8% from RMB2.8 billion in the second quarter of
2026. | · | Vehicle margin was 15.3% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with 15.5% in the third quarter
of 2025 and 9.4% in the second quarter of 2026. The decrease in vehicle margin over the third quarter of 2025 was mainly due to a different
product mix, partially offset by estimated costs related to the recall of Li MEGA in the third quarter of 2025. The increase in vehicle
margin over the second quarter of 2026 was mainly attributable to a different product mix. | · | Gross margin was 16.7% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with 16.3% in the third quarter of
2025 and 11.0% in the second quarter of 2026. | 
 Operating Expenses 
 | · | Operating expenses were RMB5.5 billion (US$822.7 million) in the third quarter of 2026, representing
a decrease of 2.3% from RMB5.6 billion in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 7.4% from RMB5.1 billion in the second quarter
of 2026. | · | Research and development expenses were RMB3.1 billion (US$464.9 million) in the third quarter of
2026, representing an increase of 4.8% from RMB3.0 billion in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 12.3% from RMB2.8 billion in
the second quarter of 2026. Research and development expenses remained relatively stable over the third quarter of 2025. The increase
in research and development expenses over the second quarter of 2026 was mainly due to increased costs to support expanding product portfolios
and technologies. | · | Selling, general and administrative expenses were RMB2.4 billion (US$352.2 million) in the third
quarter of 2026, representing a decrease of 14.7% from RMB2.8 billion in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 3.7% from RMB2.3
billion in the second quarter of 2026. The decrease in selling, general and administrative expenses over the third quarter of 2025 was
primarily due to decreased employee compensation and rental and other expenses associated with sales and servicing network. The selling,
general and administrative expenses remained relatively stable over the second quarter of 2026. | 
 6 
 Loss from Operations 
 | · | Loss from operations was RMB699.6 million (US$104.4 million) in the third quarter of 2026, representing
a decrease of 40.6% from RMB1.2 billion in the third quarter of 2025 and a decrease of 69.6% from RMB2.3 billion in the second quarter
of 2026. Operating margin was negative 2.4% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with negative 4.3% in the third quarter of 2025
and negative 9.0% in the second quarter of 2026. Non-GAAP loss from operations was RMB502.8 million (US$75.0 million) in the third
quarter of 2026, representing a decrease of 44.9% from RMB912.5 million in the third quarter of 2025 and a decrease of 76.0% from RMB2.1
billion in the second quarter of 2026. | 
 Net Loss and Net Loss Per Share 
 | · | Net loss was RMB309.7 million (US$46.2 million) in the third quarter of 2026, representing a decrease
of 50.4% from RMB624.4 million in the third quarter of 2025 and a decrease of 81.8% from RMB1.7 billion in the second quarter of 2026.
 Non-GAAP net loss was RMB112.9 million (US$16.8 million) in the third quarter of 2026, representing a decrease of 68.6% from RMB359.7
million in the third quarter of 2025 and a decrease of 92.5% from RMB1.5 billion in the second quarter of 2026. | · | Basic and diluted net loss per ADS attributable to ordinary shareholders were both RMB0.32 (US$0.05)
in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB0.62 in the third quarter of 2025 and RMB1.69 in the second quarter of 2026. Non-GAAP
basic and diluted net loss per ADS attributable to ordinary shareholders were both RMB0.12 (US$0.02) in the third quarter of 2026,
compared with RMB0.36 in the third quarter of 2025 and RMB1.49 in the second quarter of 2026. | 
 Cash Position, Operating Cash Flow and Free Cash Flow 
 | · | Cash position 7 was RMB88.2 billion (US$13.2 billion) as of September 30, 2026. | · | Net cash provided by operating activities was RMB3.2 billion (US$481.6 million) in the third quarter
of 2026, compared with RMB7.4 billion net cash used in operating activities in the third quarter of 2025 and RMB15.0 million net cash
provided by operating activities in the second quarter of 2026. The change in net cash provided by operating activities over the third
quarter of 2025 was mainly due to the decrease in payments made for inventory purchases. The change in net cash provided by operating
activities over the second quarter of 2026 was mainly due to the increase in cash received from customers mainly resulting from a higher
average selling price. | · | Free cash flow was RMB2.0 billion (US$292.6 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with
negative RMB8.9 billion in the third quarter of 2025 and negative RMB1.3 billion in the second quarter of 2026. | 
 7 Cash position includes
cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash, time deposits and short-term investments, and long-term time deposits and financial instruments
included in long-term investments. 
 7 
 Business Outlook 
 For the fourth quarter of 2026, the Company expects:
 | · | Deliveries of vehicles to be between 110,000 and 115,000 vehicles, representing a year-over-year
increase of 0.7% to 5.3%. | · | Total revenues to be between RMB31.7 billion (US$4.7 billion) and RMB33.1 billion (US$4.9 billion),
representing a year - over-year increase of 10.1% to 15.1%. | 
 This business outlook reflects the Company’s
current and preliminary views on its business situation and market conditions, which are subject to change.

 Recent Developments 
 Delivery Update 
 | · | In October 2026, the Company delivered 29,025 vehicles. As of October 31, 2026, in China, the Company
had 481 retail stores in 159 cities, 527 servicing centers and Li Auto-authorized servicing shops operating in 217 cities, and 4,206 super
charging stations in operation equipped with 23,163 charging stalls. | 
 Product Lineup Update 
 | · | In September and October 2026, the Company launched the new Li MEGA, a high-tech flagship MPV, Li i9,
a pioneering flagship family SUV, and 2026 Li i6, a pioneering five-seat SUV. These models feature the Company’s latest proprietary
technologies, including the MACH M100 chip and Lianshan Battery, together with other premium configurations. The new Li MEGA, Li i9, and
2026 Li i6 are priced at RMB509,800, RMB369,800, and RMB249,800, respectively. Deliveries of the new Li MEGA and Li i9 began in September,
and deliveries of the 2026 Li i6 began in October. | 
 Equity Financing for Chip Business 
 | · | On October 16, 2026, the Company announced the equity financing for Shanghai Mahe Xin Technology Co.,
Ltd. (“MHX Technology”), a subsidiary of the Company dedicated to its chip and domain controller business. The Company, through
a wholly-owned subsidiary, and external investors will invest RMB1.0 billion and RMB625 million respectively in MHX Technology. Further
details are available in the Company’s announcement published on the website of HKEX on October 16, 2026. | 
 US$1.0 Billion Share Repurchase Program 
 | · | Pursuant to its US$1.0 billion share repurchase program announced on March 24, 2026, the Company repurchased
a total of 10,638,200 Class A ordinary shares at an aggregate consideration of HK$493.3 million on the HKEX and a total of 13,562,312
ADSs (representing 27,124,624 Class A ordinary shares) at an aggregate consideration of US$169.7 million on the Nasdaq in the third quarter
of 2026. As of the date of this press release, the Company has repurchased a total of approximately 102.3 million Class A ordinary shares
(including approximately 23.7 million ADSs) for an aggregate consideration of approximately US$694.4 million. | 
 Global Expansion 
 | · | The Company reached new globalization milestones, launching its all-new Li L9 in the UAE in September
2026, making its European premiere at the Paris Motor Show in October 2026, and signing agreements with partners across Hong Kong, Thailand,
Singapore, the Philippines, and Vietnam in November 2026 to advance its Asia-Pacific expansion. The Company plans to debut the right-hand-drive
Li MEGA at the Thailand International Motor Expo and launch it in Hong Kong in December 2026, followed by the start of deliveries of Li
6 (the Europe-spec Li i6) in the Netherlands and Norway in the first quarter of 2027. | 
 Power Day 
 | · | In October 2026, the Company hosted Power Day to introduce its proprietary Lianshan Electric Technology
System, covering battery, electric drive, and charging infrastructure. The Company also launched the Lianshan Battery Warranty Program
at the event, further underscoring its commitment to user experience and confidence in its proprietary electric technologies. | 
 4 
 CEO and CFO Comments 
 Mr. Xiang Li, chairman and chief executive officer
of Li Auto, commented, “The strength of our proprietary technologies, from the MACH M100 chip to the Lianshan Battery, is increasingly
reinforcing our competitive moat. Through our user-centric, integrated software-hardware iteration, these capabilities enable tighter
system integration that delivers differentiated user experiences while enhancing our supply chain resilience. This ultimately translated
into stronger delivery performance in the third quarter. Looking ahead, we remain committed to advancing frontier technologies to transform
user experiences and drive industry progress.”
 Mr. Tie Li, chief financial officer of Li Auto,
added, “Despite ongoing industry-wide cost headwinds, our gross margin continued to improve sequentially, reaching 16.7% in the
third quarter, and free cash flow turned positive. This performance reflects the strength of our optimized product mix, the efficiency
gains from our proprietary technologies, and continued operational discipline. With an updated product lineup and ongoing advancements
in our in-house technologies, we are well-positioned to navigate market dynamics and further strengthen our financial performance. Going
forward, we will maintain our steadfast investments in deepening our technological moat and advancing global expansion, driving our next
phase of growth and creating incremental shareholder value.”

 Financial Results for the Third Quarter of 2026 
 Revenues 
 | · | Total revenues were RMB28.8 billion (US$4.3 billion) in the third quarter of 2026, representing
an increase of 5.4% from RMB27.4 billion in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 12.3% from RMB25.7 billion in the second quarter
of 2026. | · | Vehicle sales were RMB27.1 billion (US$4.0 billion) in the third quarter of 2026, representing
an increase of 4.7% from RMB25.9 billion in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 12.6% from RMB24.1 billion in the second quarter
of 2026. The increase in revenue from vehicle sales over the third quarter of 2025 was primarily due to the increase in vehicle deliveries,
partially offset by a lower average selling price due to a different product mix. The increase in revenue from vehicle sales over the
second quarter of 2026 was primarily attributable to a higher average selling price due to a different product mix. | · | Other sales and services were RMB1.7 billion (US$259.6 million) in the third quarter of 2026, representing
an increase of 16.2% from RMB1.5 billion in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 8.8% from RMB1.6 billion in the second quarter
of 2026. The increase in revenue from other sales and services over the third quarter of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026 was mainly
due to increased provision of services and sales of accessories, which is in line with higher accumulated vehicle sales. | 
 Cost of Sales and Gross Margin 
 | · | Cost of sales was RMB24.0 billion (US$3.6 billion) in the third quarter of 2026, representing an
increase of 4.9% from RMB22.9 billion in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 5.2% from RMB22.8 billion in the second quarter
of 2026. The increase in cost of sales over the third quarter of 2025 was primarily due to the increase in vehicle deliveries and a higher
average cost of sales due to a different product mix, partially offset by estimated costs related to the recall of Li MEGA in the third
quarter of 2025. The increase in cost of sales over the second quarter of 2026 was primarily attributable to a higher average cost of
sales due to a different product mix. | · | Gross profit was RMB4.8 billion (US$718.3 million) in the third quarter of 2026, representing an
increase of 7.8% from RMB4.5 billion in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 69.8% from RMB2.8 billion in the second quarter of
2026. | · | Vehicle margin was 15.3% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with 15.5% in the third quarter
of 2025 and 9.4% in the second quarter of 2026. The decrease in vehicle margin over the third quarter of 2025 was mainly due to a different
product mix, partially offset by estimated costs related to the recall of Li MEGA in the third quarter of 2025. The increase in vehicle
margin over the second quarter of 2026 was mainly attributable to a different product mix. | · | Gross margin was 16.7% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with 16.3% in the third quarter of
2025 and 11.0% in the second quarter of 2026. | 
 Operating Expenses 
 | · | Operating expenses were RMB5.5 billion (US$822.7 million) in the third quarter of 2026, representing
a decrease of 2.3% from RMB5.6 billion in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 7.4% from RMB5.1 billion in the second quarter
of 2026. | · | Research and development expenses were RMB3.1 billion (US$464.9 million) in the third quarter of
2026, representing an increase of 4.8% from RMB3.0 billion in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 12.3% from RMB2.8 billion in
the second quarter of 2026. Research and development expenses remained relatively stable over the third quarter of 2025. The increase
in research and development expenses over the second quarter of 2026 was mainly due to increased costs to support expanding product portfolios
and technologies. | · | Selling, general and administrative expenses were RMB2.4 billion (US$352.2 million) in the third
quarter of 2026, representing a decrease of 14.7% from RMB2.8 billion in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 3.7% from RMB2.3
billion in the second quarter of 2026. The decrease in selling, general and administrative expenses over the third quarter of 2025 was
primarily due to decreased employee compensation and rental and other expenses associated with sales and servicing network. The selling,
general and administrative expenses remained relatively stable over the second quarter of 2026. |
